subject: research/simdesign-gaugebudget
professional: a senior FE / structural-optimisation analyst (the reviewer for a stress-constrained shape-optimisation paper in Structural and Multidisciplinary Optimization); first checks: is the stress constraint mesh-converged, does the solver match beam theory, is the optimiser exploiting discretisation error, and are the per-gauge masses and prices traceable to the committed results.

evidence.correctness: Bookkeeping is exact: an independent closed-form area script (/tmp/claude-0/audit-gaugebudget/indep.py, L*w + (H-w)*w + r^2(1-pi/4), no subject import) reproduces every feasible mass in results.json to 1e-4 g and every price, mean, sd and range in both budget tables (base 1.145 1.054 0.990 0.994 1.054, mean 1.047 sd 0.063; big mean 1.037 sd 0.025). Rerunning three sub-searches (seed 0 gauge 3, seed 0 gauge 2, seed 2 gauge 2, base budget) reproduces 41.01 g / infeasible / 33.32 g exactly. The solver itself is right on a fine mesh: at h=0.6 the extrapolated outer-fibre stress of a w=12 b=4 arm is 79.13 / 75.03 MPa against beam theory 6M/(bw^2) +- F/(wb) = 79.17 / 75.00. But the headline designs are not feasible: the elementary beam stress of the 33.29 g gauge-2 design (w 14.38, b 2) is 109.0 MPa against the 100 MPa limit, and all five 33.3-33.5 g designs read 107.8-109.7 MPa by that one-line formula; FE peak for the same design rises 99.99 (h 2.5) -> 117.8 (1.25) -> 129.8 MPa (0.6). So the masses and prices are right for the h=2.5 mesh and wrong as statements about the bracket.
evidence.completeness: `python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 8 passed in 5.7 s (README says 8). experiments/figure.py regenerates mass_vs_gauge.svg byte-identically. run.py (15 min) not rerun in full; three of its 90 sub-search tasks reproduced exactly. Every README results bullet matches results.txt (checked line by line). The fine-mesh path crashes: solve(h=0.3) raises TypeError because make_mesh sets d=None above 4e7 pairs; the README does not claim a fine-mesh check, so this is a gap rather than a broken claim. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-gaugebudget/ returned 000 from this container (not verified).
evidence.verification: 8 tests pass, all smoke-level. quality_mutate.py, 5 seeded mutants in core logic, 5 survived: optimise() keeping the heaviest feasible gauge (optimise.py:39), dropping the plane-stress lambda correction (model.py:102, i.e. plane strain), zeroing the stock-thickness rule (dfm.py:109), BARRIER 500 -> 0 (optimise.py:9), doubling shear stress (model.py:128). No test compares against an analytic result, and no test exercises optimise() or run.py's summary.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, measures.py, dfm.py, optimise.py, run.py, figure.py, the test file. Engine copied from simdesign-filletfloor minus the 2026-11-18 quality fix (_min_dist), so the d=None crash at fine meshes persists here (model.py:71). Dead code in solve: `fb = basis.boundary(...) if False else None` and an unused `fb = ... if hasattr(...)` (model.py:105,107). pyproject description is copied from the patch-measure project. run.py is clear, parallel, and writes both JSON and text; figure parses results.txt rather than retyping.
evidence.claims: Every number in the README results table and bullets is backed by results.txt (pass, ten checks). Consistency with simdesign-filletfloor holds (its results.txt:3 gives the same five prices). 'About four times the evaluations' holds (FE evaluations 20,282 vs 5,032 rules, 13,644 vs 3,506 twin). Not backed: '33.3 g is a repeatable optimum that other seeds miss' and 'more budget helps' read search-mesh artefacts as properties of the design problem; the sibling simdesign-gaugemesh already showed 0 of 39 gauge-2 designs stay feasible at h <= 1.5 and simdesign-gaugescatter's README carries a 'superseded on a finer mesh' note, while this README cites neither. The limitation 'no fine-mesh check' is disclosed, which keeps this above 1.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could not build on the result: the quantity studied (seed scatter of the gauge-2 optimum under the peak element stress at h=2.5) is a discretisation artefact, and at h=2.5 the objective is discontinuous because every design is remeshed: peak stress jumps 98.7 -> 113.1 MPa for a 0.02 mm change in w (/tmp/claude-0/audit-gaugebudget/noise.py), so 'several nearby optima' cannot be told from remeshing noise. Nearest prior work: stress-constrained shape and topology optimisation (Duysinx and Bendsoe 1998, IJNME 43:1453; Le et al. 2010, SMO 41:605) and evolutionary optimisation under noisy objectives (Jin and Branke 2005, IEEE TEVC 9:303): that a DE with ~150 evaluations per gauge is seed-dependent on a noisy constraint is well known, none of this is cited, and the project is not part of a PROGRAMMES.md programme. Not new; not sound as a statement about the bracket.
evidence.domain: An FE analyst would check mesh convergence of the governing stress before reading anything into the optimum; here the constraint is the maximum element-centroid von Mises at h=2.5 mm, which under-reads even the nominal beam stress by ~9% for the gauge-2 designs and the peak by ~30% (129.8 MPa at h=0.6). The optimiser with more budget finds more of that under-read (four of five big-budget seeds land on the w~14.4 designs at ~109 MPa nominal), so 'more budget helps' is the search exploiting discretisation error. Standard practice (convergence study of the constraint, a fixed or adaptive mesh with smooth dependence on parameters, p-norm or patch aggregation) is not followed in this project.

defects.what: The headline reading ('33.3 g is a repeatable optimum that other seeds miss', 'more budget helps', scatter localised to gauge 2) is an artefact of the h=2.5 mm search mesh: the 33.29 g design carries 109.0 MPa by the one-line beam formula against the 100 MPa limit and 129.8 MPa at h=0.6; more budget finds more of the mesh under-read. simdesign-gaugemesh had already shown 0/39 gauge-2 designs feasible at finer meshes; the README neither cites it nor says the results hold only for the search mesh.

5 of 5 seeded mutants in core logic survive (optimise keeps heaviest gauge, plane strain instead of plane stress, stock rule off, barrier off, shear doubled): no analytic test of the solver and no test of optimise()'s selection.

make_mesh sets d=None when grid*boundary pairs >= 4e7, so solve() raises TypeError at h <= ~0.3 mm; the fix landed in simdesign-filletfloor on 2026-11-18 but was not carried into this copy, which blocks the fine-mesh check the README lists as missing.

Each design is remeshed, so the search-mesh objective is discontinuous in (w, r): peak stress jumps 98.7 -> 113.1 MPa for a 0.02 mm change in w at h=2.5. The 'several nearby optima' hypothesis cannot be separated from remeshing noise, and no noisy-optimisation or stress-constrained-optimisation prior work is cited.
pyproject description is copied from the patch-measure project ('Does a patch-averaged stress measure change the mass price ...').
Dead code in solve(): `fb = basis.boundary(...) if False else None` and an unused `fb = basis.boundary(facets=...) if hasattr(...)`.

verdict: Below the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 1; median 2). The bookkeeping is faithful: closed-form masses and every price, mean and sd reproduce from results.json, three sub-searches rerun exactly, the figure regenerates byte-identically, and the FE solver matches beam theory to 0.1% on a fine mesh. But the study reads a coarse-mesh artefact as a property of the design problem: the 33.29 g 'repeatable optimum' is over the 100 MPa limit by a one-line beam formula (109.0 MPa) and reads 129.8 MPa at h=0.6, the objective jumps 14 MPa for a 0.02 mm change in w because each design is remeshed, and the sibling simdesign-gaugemesh had already shown no gauge-2 design survives mesh refinement. All five seeded mutants survive, the fine-mesh path crashes (a fix the parent project has was not copied), and no prior work on noisy or stress-constrained optimisation is cited.
